blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Negotiating in the British style means playing a longer, quieter game. British negotiators rarely open with their best offer, but they also rarely open with a bad one. They start somewhere reasonable and let the conversation move gradually. Large, dramatic moves are treated with suspicion: they make Brits wonder what the other side is not saying.

Silences are used more than newcomers expect. A British negotiator may go quiet for several seconds after a proposal, simply to think. If you fill that silence with more concessions, you are giving away value for no reason.

Above all, the aim is an agreement that both sides can still defend to their own boss a week later. A deal that one side feels tricked into is not a deal — it is a problem waiting to happen.

items.q: How does a British negotiator typically make their opening offer?
items.why: "They start somewhere reasonable and let the conversation move gradually."

items.q: According to the text, how do British negotiators react to large, dramatic moves?
options: They welcome them as a sign of confidence
items.why: "Large, dramatic moves are treated with suspicion."

items.q: What is described as the ultimate aim of the negotiation?
options: The lowest possible price for one side
A deal that impresses the other side
An agreement both sides can still defend to their boss a week later
A quick deal signed in the first round
items.why: "the aim is an agreement that both sides can still defend to their own boss a week later."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The best negotiators keep filling silence with new concessions.
Silence during a negotiation can simply be thinking time.
Moving gradually is preferable to a dramatic opening.
A deal one side feels tricked into can cause problems later.
items.why: Inferência: o texto avisa que preencher o silêncio com concessões é abrir mão de valor sem motivo.

items.q: The phrase "a problem waiting to happen" suggests that…
options: a one-sided deal will eventually create trouble
the British always renegotiate their deals
problems are unavoidable in any negotiation
items.why: Inferência: um acordo em que um lado se sentiu enganado não se sustenta e volta como problema.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver preparando um colega para a segunda rodada de negociação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before we go back in tomorrow, let me tell you what I think is really going on. You came out of the first round worried because their lead went quiet on you — long pauses, almost no reaction to your numbers. I know it feels like they were unhappy, but with a British partner that is usually just how they think.

Here is the mistake I do not want you to make. Last time, when they fell silent, you dropped the price twice to keep things moving. They never asked for that. You gave away value for nothing, and now they expect the same tomorrow.

So this round, hold your nerve. Make one reasonable opening, then stop and wait. If they go quiet, let them. Count to ten in your head if you have to, but do not sweeten the offer just to fill the gap.

And keep one thing in mind. Whatever we agree, their director has to defend it to his own board next week, and so does ours. If either side walks away feeling cornered, the deal will fall apart before the ink is dry. We want something that still looks sensible seven days from now.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did the colleague come out of the first round worried?
options: The meeting ran out of time
The British partner rejected every number
The partner made a dramatic counter-offer
The British lead went quiet and barely reacted
items.why: "their lead went quiet on you — long pauses, almost no reaction to your numbers."

items.q: What mistake did the colleague make in the first round?
options: They dropped the price twice to fill the silence
They refused to make any offer
items.why: "when they fell silent, you dropped the price twice to keep things moving. They never asked for that."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "hold your nerve"?
options: Stay calm and do not rush to make concessions
Push hard for a quick agreement
Refuse to make any offer at all
items.why: Inferência: fazer uma oferta razoável e esperar, sem ceder só para preencher o silêncio.

items.q: Why does Oliver mention the director defending the deal to the board next week?
options: To suggest they should delay the negotiation
To stress that both sides need a deal they can still justify later
To warn that the board will reject any deal
To show the deadline is next week
items.why: Inferência: o acordo tem de fazer sentido para os dois lados uma semana depois, senão desmorona.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's advice overall?
options: Indifferent — the outcome does not matter
Patient and disciplined — stay steady and protect value
items.why: Inferência: ele orienta a manter a calma, não ceder à toa e buscar um acordo durável.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Their opening offer was reasonable, not their final position." An opening offer is…
options: the first proposal that starts the negotiation
the last figure put on the table
items.why: Opening offer = oferta inicial, aquela que abre a negociação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every time you make a ___, ask for something in return."
items.why: Concession = concessão: algo que você cede na negociação.

items.q: "A sudden 40% cut looked like a dramatic move." A dramatic move is…
options: a large, sudden change of position
a written summary of the deal
items.why: Dramatic move = movimento drástico, uma mudança grande e repentina.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He felt ___ into signing, and the relationship never recovered."
items.why: Tricked into = enganado a fazer algo — a pessoa sentiu que foi ludibriada.

items.q: "By cutting the price for no reason, you gave away value." To give away here means to…
options: surrender value without getting anything back
items.why: To give away = abrir mão, ceder valor sem receber nada em troca.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em negociações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Both directors still have to sign off on the final terms." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two of their people pushed back on our timeline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the plan, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, ninguém levou.

items.q: "Let's not give ground just because they go quiet." To give ground means to…
options: make concessions or retreat from your position
items.why: Give ground = ceder terreno, recuar da própria posição.

items.q: "A rushed price cut won't move the needle on trust." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
